docs.oriented.component: `Oriented` says whose axes a node's turn is measured against. `world` — the default — is the
ordinary case: the node is turned relative to the DESK, and an owner's turn reaches it through
the chain exactly as `z` does. `viewer` is the billboard.
```ts
import { node, Bounded, Oriented } from "game-kit"
const badge = node("badge",
Bounded({ bounds: rect(1.5, 0.9) }),
Oriented({ orientation: "viewer" }))
## `viewer` is a terminator, not another term
A node framed to the onlooker is indifferent to how the desk and its owners are turned, so it
does not inherit the accumulated turn AT ALL:
world  : own + Σ(the owners' angles)
viewer : own − the camera's rotation
Partial inheritance was the rejected middle — it would produce a turn nobody ordered. "Straight
relative to a turned slot" is already expressible as an own angle of 0 and needs no field.
The formula lives in ONE place, `resolveAngle`, so no call site improvises. There is no camera
yet, so the `viewer` branch is the node's own angle: the chain is severed and nothing is
subtracted.
## The field comes from the owner
`orientation` is `fromOwner`: the nearest set value up the chain wins. A tray can frame
everything it holds to the onlooker, and one badge inside it can still opt back out.
docs.oriented.billboard: Turn the tray and watch the two tokens disagree. Both sit in the same turned container with the
same own angle of zero. The left one rides the tray round; the right one is framed to the
onlooker and stays put, whatever the tray does. Set `orientation` back to `world` and they
become indistinguishable — which is the point: the frame is only visible as a difference.
